answer: Latent Fingerprint Prism. Each agent derives a key from a fixed public random seed and its own execution trace, so a duplicate agent produces a near-identical trace and thus a visible near-collision in a shared trellis of hashed trace samples. Replicas cluster on that reef of overlapping samples, revealing the operator. An attacker must generate genuinely distinct, costly execution histories per identity, paying full compute and storage to avoid detection.
